subject: Platform switch deferral & capacity tradeoff — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@cartly.io>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cartly.io, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Platform evaluation — capacity questions and timeline

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering lead had a few follow-ups after reviewing the perf reports: if we commit to a 6-month extension now, can Redwood guarantee the latency profile for 50M tokens/day during our peak month? The competing vendor told us they can meet 95th percentile <120ms with proactive shard allocation, which is close to what we need.

Two asks from our side to move this forward:
- A short benchmark run that mirrors our mix (short chat + document embed calls) — ideally over a 48-hour window.
- A draft of a term amendment that includes a 6-month extension and a capacity uplift clause (we may need +40% tokens in Q1).

We'd like to wrap internal approvals by Oct 22. Can Redwood support the benchmark next week?

Emma
Senior Product Ops
Cartly Inc

---
Attachment: cartly-workload-sample.json (sample request mix, 12KB)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Emma Li <emma@cartly.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Platform evaluation — capacity questions and timeline

Emma — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes on the benchmark; yes on a draft term amendment. Longer:

1) Benchmark scope and logistics- We can run a focused 48-hour benchmark against a model variant that's representative of your production traffic. We'll simulate the short chat + embedding mix you sent and include continuous KV cache behavior so it reflects real latency. Desired start window: Oct 18–19. Will that work on your side?

2) Performance target and fallbacks- Our ops team will run multi-tenant and dedicated runs. For the dedicated path (reserved pool), our 95th percentile target is typically <110ms for mixes like yours at the +40% uplift you described. For hosted/shared routing, we can hit <140ms but we'd propose a burst-dedicated policy to protect peak windows.

3) Terms and capacity uplift- I'll attach a draft amendment that adds a 6-month term extension, a committed baseline, and an uplift band with step-in pricing for +20% / +40% / +60% tiers. We also propose a short SLA credit if average 95p latency exceeds the committed target during the benchmark month.

Next steps proposed:
- Redwood runs the benchmark Oct 18–19 (we'll schedule exact start/end).
- You (Cartly) confirm the workload file and identify a procurement contact for the amendment.
- We share the draft amendment and MAP (mutual action plan) by Oct 15 so legal can triage.

I'll loop in Ops to validate the run plan once you confirm.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-scale-benchmarks-2027Q3.pdf (summary of previous benchmark methodology and results)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Emma Li <emma@cartly.io>, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2027 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Platform evaluation — capacity questions and timeline

Emma — Ben from Solutions here. Quick operational notes to set expectations for the Oct 18 run: 

- We'll provision a reserved pool for the test to get clean tail-latency numbers; that avoids noisy neighbors.
- We'll run three load points over 48 hours: baseline (current prod load), +40%, and a stress spike (~+80% for 1 hour) so you can see degradation characteristics.
- We'll capture token-level cost, 95/99p latency, and KV hit rates. Expect a results deck within 24 hours after the run completes.

Couple of asks from us:
- Please confirm the time zone for your on-call and whether Cartly can provide a short-term debug endpoint for trace correlation.
- If procurement wants a purchase order to hold capacity, send that to procurement@redwood.com and we'll attach it to the MAP.

I'll also include run configs in the MAP draft. 

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)

From: Emma Li <emma@cartly.io>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cartly.io, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Platform evaluation — capacity questions and timeline

Thanks, team — appreciate the quick turnaround and level of detail. A few confirmations and small asks before you run the benchmark: 

- Oct 18–19 works for the technical run window; our on-call will be Sam Park (sam.park@cartly.io) in PST.
- We can provide the debug endpoint and a short-lived PO to hold the reserved pool; procurement will issue the PO and DocuSign the amendment if the results align with the SLA language.
- Two negotiation points from Procurement:
  1) If Redwood's dedicated pool doesn't meet the <120ms 95p floor during the benchmark, Cartly expects a one-time credit equal to 10% of the monthly committed spend for the following billing month.
  2) For the +40% uplift band, Procurement requests a fixed token unit price (no step pricing) for the first three months of the uplift.

If you can include the proposed language in the MAP and amendment, procurement can fast-track review. Targeting final sign by Oct 29.

I'll wait for the MAP and amendment on Oct 15 as discussed.

Emma Li
Senior Product Ops, Cartly Inc

---
Attachment: mutual-action-plan-cartly.xlsx (MAP with milestones and acceptance criteria)
